Done. Saved both a skill section and a compact memory note.

What this question exposed (generalizable):

1. New question category — parametric VaR. "One-year lower-tail portfolio loss exceeded with 1% probability" is a Gaussian Value-at-Risk computation, not a plain lookup. None of the prior transform wrappers covered it.

2. The actual error — dropped the drift term. The correct loss is z·σ − μ, not z·σ alone. My answer (20602) was exactly 4.18× the gold (4928), and that factor = z·σ/(z·σ − μ), which is the signature of omitting the mean. Because the mutual-fund Treasury holdings grew strongly 2000→2004, the positive drift μ cancels ~76% of the z·σ band — so the true loss is far smaller. I also likely should have used the std of year-over-year changes, not the std of the 5 raw levels.

3. Reusable diagnostic — a VaR answer that's ~3-5× too large vs gold almost always means the drift term was dropped (or z·σ was computed on levels instead of mean-subtracted changes).

4. FX wrinkle — compute the loss in USD first, then multiply by the foreign-units-per-USD monthly NSA rate (first-of-month convention), then round to the requested unit.

Both the full method (with Python recipe) and the diagnostic are now in the officeqa-treasury-bulletin skill, plus a compact pointer in memory.
